record.original_question: For all integers k≥3 and 1≤ℓ≤k−1, is the minimum number sat(n,k,ℓ) of edges in an ℓ-Hamiltonian-saturated k-uniform hypergraph on n vertices of order Θ(n^ℓ)?

evidence.quote: Together, we proved that for all k ≥ 3 and ` = 1, as well as for all 4/5 k ≤ ` ≤ k − 1 sat(n, k, `) = Θ(n`) , and conjectured that (2) holds for all k and 1 ≤ ` ≤ k−1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k ≥ 3 be an integer and let 1 ≤ ℓ ≤ k − 1. A k-uniform hypergraph is a pair (V, E) where E is a set of k-element subsets of V. An ℓ-overlapping Hamiltonian cycle in a k-uniform hypergraph on n vertices (where (k − ℓ) divides n) is a cyclic ordering v_1, v_2, …, v_n of the vertices together with a sequence of edges e_1, e_2, …, e_{n/(k−ℓ)} such that each e_i consists of k consecutive vertices in the ordering and consecutive edges e_i, e_{i+1} share exactly ℓ vertices (indices taken cyclically).

A k-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices is called ℓ-Hamiltonian-saturated if H contains no ℓ-overlapping Hamiltonian cycle, but for every non-edge f ∉ E(H) (i.e., every k-subset of V(H) not already in E(H)), the hypergraph H + f does contain an ℓ-overlapping Hamiltonian cycle.

Define sat(n, k, ℓ) to be the minimum number of edges in an ℓ-Hamiltonian-saturated k-uniform hypergraph on n vertices (taken over admissible n).

Question: Is it true that for every integer k ≥ 3 and every integer ℓ with 1 ≤ ℓ ≤ k − 1,
   sat(n, k, ℓ) = Θ(n^ℓ)
as n → ∞ (through admissible values)?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture sat(n,k,ℓ) = Θ(n^ℓ) has been verified in several ranges: for ℓ = 1, for ℓ ∈ {k/2, k−1}, for the upper range 0.8k ≤ ℓ ≤ k−1, and extended to the lower-middle range (k−1)/3 ≤ ℓ < (k−1)/2 (Ruciński and collaborators; arXiv:2111.05020). The full conjecture for all 1 ≤ ℓ ≤ k−1 remains open in the intermediate ranges not covered by these results.

status_evidence.title: Constructing sparsest ℓ-hamiltonian saturated k-uniform hypergraphs for a wide range of ℓ
status_evidence.snippet: The authors extend the validity of the conjecture to the lower-middle range (k−1)/3 ≤ ℓ < (k−1)/2, showing it remains open for other intermediate values.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture confirmed for additional ranges; still open for intermediate ℓ.

status_evidence.title: On the minimum size of hamiltonian saturated hypergraphs (Ruciński et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: sat(n,k,ℓ) = Θ(n^ℓ) was proven for ℓ = 1 and for 0.8k ≤ ℓ ≤ k−1.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier ranges where the conjecture is known.
